data: 555 smoke and soot tests (SAME, SAME-R, SPICE), all at 21% O₂ and 1 atm. SAME-R's page notes microgravity smoke particles may be larger and fool detectors; an earlier flight showed the Shuttle detector missing smoke it caught in 1 g.
next_gen: Calibrate detectors on smoke made in habitat air; the size shift means 1 g calibration is not enough.

data: CO₂ and helium suppression of droplet flames: 173 FLEX tests, at up to 25% O₂. The ISS replaced its CO₂ extinguishers with fine-water-mist ones, because CO₂ was unsafe with the crew's emergency breathing equipment.
next_gen: Test suppressant amounts at 30-34 % O₂ before relying on them in a habitat.

data: In still air, all 41 CFI-G flames at ≤25 % O₂ went out by themselves; at 33-40 % O₂, 30 of 91 were still burning when the fuel was cut. BRE saw emulated solids keep burning without air flow at raised O₂.
next_gen: In an oxygen-rich habitat, pair fan shutdown with active extinguishing.

data: BASS-II mapped flames starving at low air speed and blowing off at high speed (12 flame-outs). Saffire-II silicone burned in its 1 g comparison burns but not in microgravity; at lunar gravity some materials burn at lower oxygen than at 1 g (FM2 work).
next_gen: Screen habitat materials at habitat O₂, pressure, air speed and gravity, not only NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 in Earth air.

area: Air quality: scrubbers and crew masks
data: Burning acrylic (PMMA) on Cygnus raised cabin CO₂ by 8,117-8,539 ppm, several times more than fabric. In BASS-II's ISS burns, thick PMMA slabs raised CO by a median 335 ppm per burn, fabric by about 20 ppm.
investigations: Saffire VI (Urban et al. 2024, Table 2); BASS-II test matrix (PSI-25)
next_gen: Size CO₂ and CO removal and masks for plastic fires.

data: The same fabric in nearly the same air spread 1.8 mm/s in a 51 cm duct and 5.1 mm/s in a 7.6 cm duct.
investigations: Saffire I-IV, BASS; Olson et al., Table 1
next_gen: Treat racks, ducts and stowage gaps as higher-risk zones for detection and suppression.
